record.original_question: Given a term in ordinary untyped lambda calculus, is it decidable whether that term can be assigned a type in the second-order lambda-2 calculus?

evidence.quote: Given a term in ordinary untyped lambda calculus, is it decidable whether it can be typed in the second-order λ2 calculus?

artifact.status_search_result: J. B. Wells (LICS 1994; journal version Ann. Pure Appl. Logic 1999) proved that typability and type checking in the second-order λ-calculus (System F) are equivalent and undecidable, settling this long-standing open problem.

status_evidence.title: Typability and type checking in System F are equivalent and undecidable
status_evidence.snippet: Wells proved that type checking in System F is undecidable by reduction from semi-unification, and that typability is undecidable by reduction from type checking.
status_evidence.claim: Typability in System F (λ2) is undecidable.

status_evidence.title: The Undecidability of System F Typability and Type Checking for Reductionists
status_evidence.snippet: A modern exposition of the undecidability of System F typability and type checking.
status_evidence.claim: The undecidability result has been reconfirmed and re-examined in later work.
